text.content:
Storyteller-facing content. Most vampiric powers affect the vampire or the surrounding material world; Obtenebration practitioners reach outside the world into a different sort of space and bring back dark gifts. For many practitioners, the Abyss is simply the conceptual realm they draw shadow-stuff from; a handful probe deeper into layers of mystery. Intelligence exists in the Abyss but does not possess self-awareness or identity in any comprehensible sense — fragments of knowledge and passion coalesce and break apart, more like a computer capable of emotion than a sentient entity.

This is an advanced and dangerous sub-system. Storytellers should adjudicate both procedures below carefully, and reserve them for player characters who have genuinely invested in Obtenebration and Occult (Abyss) lore, per the prerequisites given.

Prerequisite: at least five dots total between Obtenebration and Occult (Abyss specialty), with at least two dots/Traits in each. Below this threshold, only pragmatic physical-world applications of Arms of the Abyss are possible — no summoning.

Arms of the Abyss can draw out a portion of the Abyss's intelligence when coupled with proper occult preparation:

  1. Conduct a one-hour ritual, spending one Blood Trait, and win an Intelligence + Occult (Static Mental Challenge, difficulty seven Traits).
  2. Then invoke Arms of the Abyss as normal (Static Social Challenge, difficulty seven Traits, per that power's own system) — but only a single arm manifests. It has the normal physical statistics of an Arms of the Abyss tentacle, plus one dot of Mental Attributes per dot/level of Obtenebration the summoner possesses (allocated as the summoner likes). Extra successes on the ritual roll, or extra Blood Traits spent at invocation, each add another dot of Mental Attributes.

The resulting Abyss creature possesses at least one powerful derangement and an obsession resembling a Path of Enlightenment sin (usually level six or higher), chosen by the Storyteller. It moves independently at the summoner's running speed and exists for the scene or one hour, whichever is shorter; intense light dispels it immediately.

Extending its presence: Repeating the ritual steps can extend the creature's presence for the rest of the night. Three ritual successes in a row grant it permanent presence, so long as the summoner feeds it (10 minus the summoner's Obtenebration rating) Blood Traits nightly.

Absorbing the creature: The summoner may try to absorb the manifestation into himself by defeating it in a Physical Challenge (reducing it to zero health levels) and draining its darkness. Success grants the summoner half the creature's dots in each Attribute for the remainder of the night, plus its derangement (this derangement cannot be resisted with Willpower).

Danger — possession: If the creature reduces its summoner to torpor, it can invade and control his body for the rest of the night. It can repeat this three nights running to fully possess him, until driven out by another Obtenebration practitioner who reduces the invaded vampire to torpor and repeats the summoning ritual to draw the intruding entity back out.

An expert in Obtenebration can enter the Abyss directly. This is the Obtenebration equivalent of Psychic Projection.

  1. Conduct the same hour-long ritual as Calling the Thing in Darkness, spending one Blood Trait, and win an Intelligence + Occult Static Mental Challenge (difficulty seven Traits).
  2. Then use Shadowstep (see the Obtenebration power of that name). If each step works, the vampire passes into the Abyss itself, risking encounters with Abyss spirits along the way.

While in the Abyss: every number of turns equal to the traveler's Obtenebration rating, the Storyteller calls for a Perception + Obtenebration Static Mental Challenge (difficulty eight Traits) to sense a coalescing fragment of Abyssal intelligence nearby. Failure means a creature (built as with the summoning procedure above, scaled to the traveler's own skill) approaches and attempts to possess the traveler. A botch means immediate possession and ejection to the nearest dark place in the material world.

Treat travel and combat mechanics in the Abyss like the astral plane used for Psychic Projection: the character can move very swiftly (up to roughly 1,000 mph in comparable terms) and can see into total darkness. If the character loses all Willpower in astral combat while in the Abyss, no silver cord is severed as with true astral projection — instead, the Abyss simply spits the character back out into the nearest dark place in the material world.
